nodes.description: Ssx1 expression was knocked down in the testes of cynomolgus monkeys, because the rodent SSX family expanded independently and mice cannot model SSX1. The knocked-down animals had reduced sperm motility and abnormal sperm morphology.

evidence.reference_title: Deficiency of primate-specific SSX1 induced asthenoteratozoospermia in infertile men and cynomolgus monkey and tree shrew models.
evidence.snippet: As the mouse model could not be used for studying SSX1, we used a non-human primate model and tree shrews, which are phylogenetically similar to primates, to knock down (KD) Ssx1 expression in the testes.

nodes.description: Testicular RNA sequencing after Ssx1 knockdown showed that many biological processes during spermatogenesis were affected. Which of them produces the sperm motility and morphology defects has not been shown.
